One thing that a lot of people do NOT understand is that ultimately the US was based on the idea of much smaller governing units. This is actually one reason why some groups get a lot of flack they really shouldn't - they aren't opposed to Idealistic Program X to fix Problem Y, they're opposed to Idealistic Program X being implemented as a one-size-fits-all, bloated Federal government solution that ends up making Problem Y much, much worse in the long term, and often will have a lot of special interests bogging it down even if it works. The result is Problem Y has a half-ass solution that costs many times more and is many times less effective than it could be.

Municipal broadband is a great example of that. If this was done on a Federal level, the result would be slow, shitty, over-regulated and probably even more privy to spying efforts. However, a municipal broadband system can address local needs and desires in a much more straightforward and efficient way.

When someone mentions "government ISP" they usually think "Welcome to USNet! Please specify desired YouTube video, your request will be processed and returned in 6-8 weeks," e.g. centralized government solution, as opposed to lots of smaller solutions that are altogether more efficient and effective.
